observations: A single solar panel leaning against a wall.
The panel has a white aluminum frame and a blue photovoltaic surface.
The surface is divided into two sections by a central horizontal bar.
Three black mounting brackets are attached to the frame.
The panel is resting on a tiled floor.
No brand name, model number, or wattage label is visible on the front of the panel.

claims.evidence: The panel is not shown with a specification label; this is the seller's word only.
The cell structure in photo 0 appears to be monocrystalline, but a clear close-up is not provided.

risks.risk: The panel may be a counterfeit or a lower wattage model.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's specification label on the back of the panel.

risks.risk: The panel may have internal cell damage or cracks.
risks.proof: A clear, close-up photo of the cell surface.

risks.risk: The panel may be non-functional or have a low output.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading the open-circuit voltage (Voc) and short-circuit current (Isc) in direct sunlight.

proof_requests: Photo of the specification label on the back of the panel.
Close-up photo of the cells to confirm monocrystalline type.
Video of a multimeter test in sunlight.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
